audit_findings.title: Null perimeter despite the completed Lawton disposition
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $312 million sale, approximately $60 million purchase, $5.1 million annual rent avoided, and approximately $300 million floating-rate debt repaid; net OE effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Historical Lawton earnings remain in the trend anchor, while the replacement facility's avoided rent and the debt-repayment interest benefit are only partially reflected in 2025 equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The sale of the Lawton Facility closed on July 25, 2025 and the Company transitioned facility operations to the Oklahoma Department of Corrections simultaneously on July 25, 2025.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter omission is demonstrated: perimeter is null even though Lawton was sold and operations ceased in July 2025. The direction is unresolved because removing Lawton lowers historical OE, while avoided rent and lower interest expense raise post-transaction OE. These filed transaction amounts are large relative to the $61.2 million anchor, so a current-perimeter rebuild could materially change the valuation.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct each historical OE year excluding Lawton, add Western Region ownership economics and avoided rent, apply post-sale interest expense, and rerun the trend anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Unreserved detainee litigation could create both senior cash claims and recurring labor costs
audit_findings.magnitude: unreserved exposure unquantified; filed Nwauzor reserve $37.6 million, equal to about $0.28 per share, 61% of anchor OE, and 4.1% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Unrecorded judgments would reduce the equity bridge or future OE; wage-rule changes and legal fees would reduce recurring OE and potentially growth.
audit_findings.evidence: GEO has not recorded any accruals relating to these lawsuits, other than in connection with the Nwauzor case discussed above, at this time as losses are not considered probable nor reasonably estimable.
audit_findings.explanation: The pending unreserved cases and absence of accruals are demonstrated, but an adverse outcome and its amount are not. The record supplies no exposure estimate or affected labor-cost base, so materiality of those cases cannot be established. Separately, the known $37.6 million Nwauzor reserve is large relative to anchor OE and requires a treatment check to prevent omission or double counting.
audit_findings.action: Obtain case-specific reasonably possible loss ranges, expected legal fees, affected detainee-work hours and wage rates; trace the $37.6 million reserve through 2025 OE and the bridge, then rerun probability-weighted claim and recurring-wage cases.

audit_findings.title: Proposed California gross-receipts tax could invalidate normalized margins
audit_findings.mechanism: If enacted, a 50% tax on affected California gross receipts beginning in 2027 would directly reduce OE, impair contract economics, and potentially force repricing, termination, or perimeter changes.
audit_findings.evidence: Furthermore, recently proposed legislation in California, Assembly Bill 1633, or AB1633, would impose an annual tax equal to 50% of the gross receipts of private detention facility operators beginning on January 1, 2027, if enacted into law.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a forward-looking legislative risk, not a demonstrated liability or current-period error. The supplied record identifies the proposed 50% rate but provides neither enacted status nor affected California revenue, reimbursement rights, or passage probability.
audit_findings.action: Monitor the bill through enactment or failure; obtain California facility revenue and contract reimbursement, repricing and termination provisions, and rerun enacted and probability-weighted cases if the legislative risk becomes operative.

audit_findings.title: Maintenance capital expenditure is underidentified during a major activation cycle
audit_findings.magnitude: filed 2026 maintenance estimate of $80-$95 million, equal to 131%-155% of the $61.2 million anchor OE; classification error unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Maintenance capex is deducted directly in OE; classifying recurring spending as growth overstates OE, while classifying activation or contract-specific growth spending as maintenance understates OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Of these projects, we estimate that approximately $80 to $95 million are related to facility maintenance costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The missing year-by-year reconciliation is a demonstrated support deficiency, although a numerical misclassification has not yet been proved. The filed maintenance range exceeds anchor OE and 2025 total capex was $197.5 million, making the classification reasonably capable of materially changing the anchor and scenario values.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile maintenance capex used in every OE year to facility maintenance, renovations, monitoring-equipment replacement, idle-facility needs and activation projects; document recurring versus growth classifications and rerun OE, the anchor and all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Captive-insurer investments may fall between the numerator and bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $84.420 million of marketable equity and fixed-income securities at June 30, 2026, about $0.63 per share and 9.2% of base equity value gross; consistent net amount unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Purged investment returns reduce OE, while excluding the supporting investments from the bridge understates value; failing to offset associated insurance claims or restricted obligations could instead overstate value.
audit_findings.evidence: Florina holds cash and investments in order to meet solvency requirements and meet financial obligations as presented, including an investment portfolio of marketable fixed income and equity securities.
audit_findings.explanation: The restricted investment balance and portfolio-income purge are demonstrated, but the record does not trace which income was removed or establish Florina's net assets after insurance obligations. The gross balance is potentially significant, yet gross investments cannot be added without matching liabilities and restrictions.
audit_findings.action: Produce a Florina-only balance sheet and income statement, identify all investment income purged from OE, match investments and cash to insurance reserves and other obligations, and rerun the bridge using only the consistent net amount.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded pension liability is a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: filed $29.568 million unfunded status at June 30, 2026, about $0.22 per share and 3.2% of the $914 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any portion not captured through forecast cash contributions should be deducted as a bridge claim ahead of common equity; otherwise value is overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: The long-term portion of the pension liability related to the defined benefit plan as of December 31, 2025 and 2024 was $28.4 million and $26.2 million, respectively, and is included in Other Non-Current liabilities in the accompanying consolidated balance sheets.
audit_findings.explanation: The unfunded obligation is demonstrated and the bridge does not identify it. A full $29.568 million deduction would reduce base value from approximately $6.80 to $6.58 per share and bull value from $7.55 to about $7.33, still roughly 77% below the $31.77 market price. It therefore cannot change the valuation conclusion on the supplied numbers.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether OE reflects pension expense or actual contributions; if settlement is not fully captured, deduct the $29.568 million unfunded status and rerun the bridge while avoiding double counting.
